R01.statement: RAID retains a project launchpad and Guild identity.

R02.statement: A project launched through RAID becomes a Guild; its authorized creator becomes the Guild Founder.

R03.statement: Holding the recognized project token establishes holder eligibility for that Guild.

R04.statement: A Raider can work across Guilds and can also be a Founder or Member.

R05.statement: Every published Raid has an E–S difficulty label and explicit skill requirements.

R06.statement: Skill rank represents demonstrated capacity, not token wealth or paid placement.

R07.statement: RAID recommends task difficulty and reward composition/range; participant routing and duration complete the proposed assistance flow.
R07.detail: C02 directly requests rank/reward; routing/duration are carried-forward additions

R08.statement: The public website has a discoverable Raid feed.

R09.statement: Paid placement exists as a clearly distinguishable visibility product.
R09.detail: C03; labeling is a trust-preserving implementation requirement

R10.statement: Guilds accumulate a reputation based on funding, payment, requirements, and treatment of contributors.

R11.statement: Sensitive work uses progressive trust and explicit access approval.

R12.statement: Skills can be claimed, evidenced, assessed, and verified independently.

R13.statement: One Raider may hold only one active Raid/work engagement at a time.

R14.statement: A high-trust Challenge may select a Raider or Party for a larger Raid.

P01.statement: Humans, registered AI agents, and AI influencers are distinct participant types.
P01.detail: Common work contracts; different proof and execution needs.

P02.detail: Every participant has consent, responsibility, capacity checks, and a payout allocation.

P03.statement: Prize-based Guild Challenges can compare multiple solutions.

P04.detail: An ongoing responsibility must not bypass the one-active rule.

P05.statement: Rewards can combine supported stablecoins, SOL, project tokens, and RAID.
P05.detail: Support follows tested adapters; “anything” is not unchecked arbitrary-token acceptance.

P06.statement: RAID token utilities may include platform services, execution credits, and paid visibility.
P06.detail: No economics or launch allocation is finalized in the available source.

P07.statement: Newcomers should have a low-risk path to earning and proving skill.
P07.detail: No forced token purchase in the proposed baseline.

P08.statement: AI assistance should reduce founder configuration work.
P08.detail: Explanations and founder control remain visible.

D01.statement: One TypeScript modular monolith, PostgreSQL, web process, background worker, and separate untrusted execution environments.
D01.detail: Keeps transactions and ownership clear without early microservices.

D02.statement: No mandatory RAID holding/staking requirement in the baseline.
D02.detail: The token/rank ladder was removed; remaining license policy is OPEN.

D03.statement: Every paid execution slot, public or private, must have fully verified reward funding before accepting commitments and verified escrow binding before work starts.
D03.detail: Selection compensation and main-Raid funding are separate obligations.

D04.statement: All confidential Raids and all B/A/S work require approval plus participant acceptance.
D04.detail: Rank alone cannot grant private access.

D05.statement: A standard Raid has one selected Raider or one Party.
D05.detail: Group microtasks use separate execution slots, not several people competing for one promised payment.

D06.statement: Build and review duties hold the active slot; a terminal work outcome releases it independently of settlement.
D06.detail: Preserves commitment without trapping workers during payment incidents.

D07.statement: Skill-specific ranks and evidence are canonical; an optional profile headline cannot override them.
D07.detail: Community activity cannot manufacture a developer qualification.

D08.statement: Use public or sanitized task material for initial onboarding and trial work.
D08.detail: Reduces required trust for first participation.

D09.statement: Initial automated recommendations use a bounded rubric; an LLM can explain or propose a structured draft.
D09.detail: Avoids pretending an unevaluated model can price every job precisely.

D10.statement: Initial sponsored placements use disclosed fixed slots; bidding is a later compatible mode.
D10.detail: Makes delivery, billing, and refunds easier to validate.

D11.statement: Exact launch protocol, custody design, program authorities, fee schedule, and token economics remain OPEN.
D11.detail: The source discussion does not finalize them.

D12.statement: Mainnet payments and trading remain disabled until their specific implementation and operating gates pass.
D12.detail: A mock or devnet flow is not a production payment system.

D13.statement: Removing a wallet or losing a token balance cannot erase completed work, assessed skills, or financial claims.
D13.detail: Adopted preservation default; not a claim that C05 explicitly settled retention mechanics.

I01.statement: The database rejects a second active engagement for the same canonical participant.

I02.statement: Party activation either reserves every participant or reserves none.

I03.statement: Every financial obligation and transfer uses integer base units and a full asset identity.

I04.statement: Cumulative paid, refunded, and remaining obligations never exceed verified credited funds for that asset.

I05.statement: A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome.

I06.statement: Private bytes never appear in public API fields, rendered page payloads, search indexes, previews, logs, or notification snippets.

I07.statement: No background score change, token sale, or service outage grants code access or confiscates a reward.

I08.statement: Every acceptance and financial decision refers to immutable terms and a specific submission/version.

I09.statement: External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana.

I10.statement: Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization.

I11.statement: Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority.

I12.statement: Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation.

G01.statement: Approved protocol, parameters, verified IDs, authority/fee behavior, recovery.

G02.statement: Defined authority, program/provider capability, reserves/claims/refunds, recovery, relevant assurance.

G03.statement: Notice, ordinary acceptance finality, objection/appeal, final decision, hold/claim race behavior.
G03.detail: All live settlement claimability, including ordinary acceptance, disputes, and Challenge awards.

G04.statement: Exact registry, decimals/program checks, extension policy, complete tested paths.

G05.statement: Supported jurisdictions/users, rights, fees, dispute operator and service scope.

G06.statement: Real authorization, effective provider grants, isolation, revocation and incident handling.

G07.statement: Operator identity, sandbox, tool authority, spend controls, provider data policy.

G08.statement: Account control, current API capability, content approval, retry/takedown/metrics rules.

G10.statement: Monitoring, staffed case ownership, backups/restore, release/incident playbooks.

AC01.statement: User connects a second wallet while holding an active Raid.
AC01.detail: Same canonical participant, same history and capacity.

AC02.statement: Reuse a wallet-login nonce or change its domain.

AC03.statement: New user completes orientation with no verified skill.
AC03.detail: Can find explicit starter tasks; no fabricated verified rank.

AC04.statement: E-ranked participant buys a large RAID balance.
AC04.detail: Skill rank and high-rank eligibility do not change.

AC05.statement: A-ranked frontend developer applies for B-ranked Solana work without that skill.
AC05.detail: Required skill fails with an actionable explanation.

AC06.statement: Experienced newcomer passes a relevant advanced assessment.
AC06.detail: Relevant skill can qualify quickly; Guild Trust/private access are still separate.

AC07.statement: Token holder attempts Guild administration or private download.

AC08.statement: RPC outage prevents refreshing holder balance.
AC08.detail: Membership observation becomes stale/unknown; no destructive inference.

AC09.statement: Related accounts farm reciprocal easy tasks.
AC09.detail: Suspect events flagged under review policy; no automatic high technical rank.

AC10.statement: Dispute finding is reversed on appeal.
AC10.detail: Attributable reputation correction without erased evidence/history.

AC11.statement: Same Raider accepts two different Raids concurrently.
AC11.detail: Exactly one commitment; other request conflicts.

AC12.statement: Two applicants accept the same available slot.
AC12.detail: Exactly one selected engagement and one funded binding.

AC13.statement: A Party contains one busy member.
AC13.detail: Entire Party commitment rolls back; no orphan engagement or partial reservation.

AC14.statement: Normal acceptance races with Challenge acceptance.
AC14.detail: One active engagement across both entry paths.

AC15.statement: Two registered agents under one capacity-limited operator accept different work.
AC15.detail: Operator transaction permits only one engagement.

AC16.statement: Human and AI members under one operator join the same allowed Party.
AC16.detail: Individual commitments coexist under one same-engagement operator reservation.

AC17.statement: An offer was generated while available, but the Raider later became busy.
AC17.detail: Offer acceptance fails current capacity checks.

AC18.statement: Public paid work has no private resources but binding is pending.
AC18.detail: Remains in setup; cannot start commissioned work.

AC19.statement: Worker submits and review/revision duty remains.
AC19.detail: Active slot stays held until bounded operational closure.

AC20.statement: Work is accepted but its payment is still pending.
AC20.detail: Capacity is released; unpaid claim remains visible.

AC21.statement: Reviewer never responds, or worker never submits.
AC21.detail: Deadline process reaches finite closure; money/fault is not decided by silence.

AC22.statement: Terminal work is reopened while the Raider has new work.
AC22.detail: No silent reactivation; new consent/capacity required.

AC23.statement: A delayed closure job arrives after the Raider starts another job.

AC24.statement: Five application targets close or offers expire.
AC24.detail: Old applications no longer consume the cap; new applications possible.

AC25.detail: New slot/terms/reservation; original history and protected claims remain intact.

AC26.statement: Client supplies unrelated successful transaction signature.
AC26.detail: No funding credit without the correct program/vault/asset/effect.

AC27.statement: RPC accepts a transaction but it never finalizes.
AC27.detail: No verified-funded/paid label; status remains accurate.

AC28.statement: Reward promises two assets; only one is deposited.
AC28.detail: Full reward is not eligible for commitment.

AC29.statement: Two mints share a ticker, or same mint address is presented on wrong network.

AC30.statement: Asset policy version changes for the same underlying asset.
AC30.detail: Existing balance is not duplicated or split into spendable new funds.

AC31.statement: Founder refunds while work binding is racing.
AC31.detail: Program serializes outcomes; if refund wins, no work/access starts.

AC33.statement: Payout times out after success and is rebuilt with a new signature.
AC33.detail: Same semantic claim cannot pay again.

AC34.statement: A shared pool funds several slots.
AC34.detail: Each reservation protected; no deposit promised twice.

AC35.statement: Work is committed but not yet reviewed/allocated.
AC35.detail: Founder cannot treat its reserve as refundable uncommitted cash.

AC36.statement: Some Party/asset claims settle and another fails.
AC36.detail: Correct partial status; only unpaid claims retried.

AC37.statement: Token transfer becomes frozen after funding.
AC37.detail: Obligation remains; blocked availability incident; no silent haircut.

AC38.detail: Hold/finality/claim serialize under policy; no contradictory spend.

AC39.statement: Operational work closes while a signed binding later finalizes.
AC39.detail: Late-binding recovery; no reopened work or automatic code grant.

AC40.statement: Unauthorized actor changes payout address or settlement beneficiaries.
AC40.detail: Rejected; proof and permitted beneficiary process required.

AC41.statement: Mainnet config contains test asset/program or mock provider.

AC42.statement: Visitor inspects private-Raid HTML, API data, search, metadata or preview.
AC42.detail: Only approved teaser; no private bytes.

AC43.statement: High-rank token holder requests a repo without approval.

AC44.statement: Founder grants one repository expecting folder secrecy.
AC44.detail: UI/config identifies actual scope; approved isolated resource required.

AC45.statement: Source Challenge grant is revoked after main-Raid grant starts on same repo.
AC45.detail: Effective reconciliation preserves the new valid access.

AC46.statement: Contributor had independent repository rights before the Raid.
AC46.detail: Removing RAID grant does not claim all access disappeared or delete unrelated rights.

AC47.statement: Provider revocation fails or old grant job arrives late.
AC47.detail: Incident/retry; stale grant cannot revive undesired access.

AC48.statement: Submission includes a malicious build script, URL, or prompt instruction.
AC48.detail: Isolation/input policy prevents unauthorized data or tool access.

AC49.statement: Account is restricted with an unsettled claim.
AC49.detail: Safe access to financial status and dispute evidence remains under policy.

AC50.statement: Party leader changes accepted split without other members.
AC50.detail: Amendment rejected until affected consents and valid funding.

AC51.statement: Valid Challenge entry does not win.
AC51.detail: Qualification/participation preserved; no automatic reliability failure.

AC52.statement: Founder changes judging weights after commitments.

AC53.statement: Four guaranteed prototype payments plus a prize are promised.
AC53.detail: Maximum qualifying liability funded before commitments.

AC54.statement: Selected Challenge builder declines main Raid.
AC54.detail: No main engagement, no penalty merely for declining, selection payment preserved.

AC55.statement: Selection-to-main handoff races with another offer or operator job.
AC55.detail: One atomic capacity outcome; no double reservation.

AC56.detail: Target closes under recovery; source compensation/history remain intact.

AC57.statement: Guild wants to use a nonwinner's private code.
AC57.detail: Requires rights already granted or a separate authorized agreement.

AC58.detail: Clear Sponsored label; no skill/reputation/judging boost.

AC59.statement: Bid loses or purchased placement cannot be delivered.

AC60.statement: Social publish request times out after provider success.

AC61.statement: AI reaches total budget across retries/subagents.
AC61.detail: Further spend blocked; no autonomous budget expansion.

AC62.statement: AI tries to approve its own output or withdraw reward.
AC62.detail: Permission denied; ordinary authorized review required.

AC63.statement: Agent changes model/version to evade failure history/capacity.
AC63.detail: Canonical identity/commitment retained; evaluation policy applies.

AC64.statement: Failed/cancelled AI run leaves an active engagement.
AC64.detail: Bounded recovery or operational closure; no indefinite slot lock.

AC65.statement: Role title is used to hide an ongoing second job.
AC65.detail: Active duty is modeled and rejected if it violates capacity.

AC66.statement: Founder launches a new project through the selected route, verifies its resulting mint, activates the Guild, funds a public Raid, and a Raider completes and claims it.
AC66.detail: Verified launch artifacts and Guild linkage, correct accepted contract and funded binding, work outcome, verified transfer and attributable reputation evidence.

AC67.statement: Process crashes after external success but before local receipt.
AC67.detail: Reconciliation records existing effect; no duplicate action.

AC68.statement: Restore after losing records newer than the last snapshot, including a new accepted engagement and completed external effect.
AC68.detail: Recover original terms, consents, semantic IDs and capacity from approved durability; reconcile before writes. If recovery fails, affected operations stay safely unavailable. No repeated effects or revived old grants.

AC69.statement: Same idempotency key is reused with a different payload.
AC69.detail: Explicit conflict; cannot overwrite original command result.

AC70.statement: Keyboard/mobile user completes the core flow with wallet rejection and retry.
AC70.detail: Draft preserved, clear focus/error/status, no duplicate engagement or funding intent.

AC71.statement: Authorized representative links an existing project/token and completes the supported funded-work flow.
AC71.detail: Project authority and canonical token verified; labeled existing-project onboarding and not counted as a new token launch.

AC72.statement: Founder/admin changes ordinary Raid reward, scope, deadline or global defaults after acceptance.
AC72.detail: Original accepted version stays effective. Material amendment needs affected consent, required additional funding and a new audited version; unilateral overwrite is rejected.

O01.detail: Typed adapter; choose one supported route first. / M3; product and Solana lead.

O02.statement: Launch supply, decimals, distribution, authorities, liquidity/curve and migration policy.
O02.detail: No invented economics; expose only selected route's supported parameters. / Real launch; Founder/product authority.

O03.statement: Real RAID token plan and utility activation.
O03.detail: Separate milestone; no presumed supply/price/allocations. / Token launch/utility; project owner.

O04.statement: Any flat RAID access license after removal of rank-linked stakes.
O04.detail: Off by default; preserve optional policy interface. / License feature; project owner.

O05.statement: Escrow provider/custom program and custody/upgrade authority.
O05.detail: Mediated candidate design with constrained authority, pending review. / Real rewards; product/Solana/security/operations.

O06.statement: Dispute mediator, quorum, notice/appeal/finality and abandoned-case recovery.
O06.detail: Bounded operations and protected claims; commercial finality must be selected. / Live settlements/awards; product/operations.

O07.statement: Initial supported assets and extension/freeze policy.
O07.detail: Small reviewed allowlist; full-identity asset model. / Each enabled payment asset; treasury/security.

O08.statement: Platform fees, launch fees, promotion prices and AI charging/refunds.
O08.detail: Exact quotes and net rewards; examples not binding. / Monetized features; product/finance.

O09.detail: Qualitative skill rubric, evidence metrics and confidence first. / Automated scoring/promotion; trust lead.

O10.statement: Selection/prize rights, stipend rules, no-qualifier/tie and appeal policy.
O10.detail: Paid bounded selection first; separate prize mode. / Challenge launch; product/legal-template owner.

O11.statement: Formal privacy, retention, account deletion and identity-attestation policy.
O11.detail: Minimal necessary data; no automatic mandatory KYC assumption. / Public operations; product/security.

O12.detail: Resolve for the actual launch/work/payment model. / Public paid operations; project owner with appropriate expertise.

O13.statement: GitHub organization/provider plans and supported grant mechanism.
O13.detail: Verify actual capability; scoped resource and effective-access reconciliation. / Confidential work; access/integration lead.

O14.statement: Model providers, data retention/training permissions, tool providers, price cards.
O14.detail: Provider-agnostic policy; explicit per-task permission. / Managed AI; execution/product lead.

O15.detail: Individual-operator pilot cap as specified; no silent scale-up. / Broader agent marketplace; product/trust.

O16.detail: Manual evidence before approved automated publishing. / Influencer automation; integration/product.

O17.statement: Sponsored auction mechanism and reserve/charge/refund rules.
O17.detail: Fixed slots first; first-price candidate remains disabled. / Bidding; product/treasury.

O18.statement: Hosting, selected package/runtime versions, provider SLOs and budgets.
O18.detail: Simple web/worker/PostgreSQL topology; verify against deployment environment. / Production release; engineering/operations.

O19.statement: Ongoing Role contracts/cadence and operator support hours.
O19.detail: One active duty period; no concurrency loophole. / Roles and live service; product/operations.

R15.statement: Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules.

R16.statement: Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project.

I13.statement: Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution.

AC73.statement: Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist.
AC73.detail: Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect.

AC74.statement: Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation.
AC74.detail: Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced.

AC75.statement: Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence.
AC75.detail: Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review.

criteria.required_evidence: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.

List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.

List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.

Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.

Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.

Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.

Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.

Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.

Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.

Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.

Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.

List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.

Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.

Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.

Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.

For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.

For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.

Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.

For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

### Explicit domain binding — Shared contracts and architecture

**Affected canonical records:** accounts, participants, terms_versions, engagements, active_commitments, assets, command_receipts, outbox_events, audit_events.

**Permission contract:** Domain owners define commands; operations have scoped repair authority; development access does not imply customer or treasury authority.

**State/effect contract:** Additive migration/backfill; immutable terms and semantic IDs survive rollback/restore; constraints and outbox are established before dependent slices.

**Adverse/recovery cases:** Legacy obligations survive migration; crash after external success; restore with missing recent acceptance; same idempotency key with altered request.

These are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.

| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |
|---|---|---|---|

| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |
| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |
| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |
| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |
| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |

### Individually reviewable criteria

Each criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.

- [ ] **E01-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.
- [ ] **E01-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.
- [ ] **E01-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.
- [ ] **E01-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.
- [ ] **E01-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.
- [ ] **E01-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.
- [ ] **E01-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.
- [ ] **E01-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.
- [ ] **E01-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.
- [ ] **E01-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.
- [ ] **E01-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.
- [ ] **E01-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.
- [ ] **E01-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.
- [ ] **E01-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.
- [ ] **E01-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **E01-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **E01-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **E01-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.

- [ ] **E01-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **E01-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **E01-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **E01-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.

Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. ### Exact applicable requirements and scenarios

| ID | Authority class | Required behavior | Qualification / expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC01 | ACCEPTANCE | User connects a second wallet while holding an active Raid. | Same canonical participant, same history and capacity. |
| AC02 | ACCEPTANCE | Reuse a wallet-login nonce or change its domain. | Authentication fails; no duplicate session/link. |
| AC03 | ACCEPTANCE | New user completes orientation with no verified skill. | Can find explicit starter tasks; no fabricated verified rank. |
| AC04 | ACCEPTANCE | E-ranked participant buys a large RAID balance. | Skill rank and high-rank eligibility do not change. |
| AC05 | ACCEPTANCE | A-ranked frontend developer applies for B-ranked Solana work without that skill. | Required skill fails with an actionable explanation. |
| AC06 | ACCEPTANCE | Experienced newcomer passes a relevant advanced assessment. | Relevant skill can qualify quickly; Guild Trust/private access are still separate. |
| AC07 | ACCEPTANCE | Token holder attempts Guild administration or private download. | Denied unless separately granted. |
| AC08 | ACCEPTANCE | RPC outage prevents refreshing holder balance. | Membership observation becomes stale/unknown; no destructive inference. |
| AC09 | ACCEPTANCE | Related accounts farm reciprocal easy tasks. | Suspect events flagged under review policy; no automatic high technical rank. |
| AC10 | ACCEPTANCE | Dispute finding is reversed on appeal. | Attributable reputation correction without erased evidence/history. |
| AC11 | ACCEPTANCE | Same Raider accepts two different Raids concurrently. | Exactly one commitment; other request conflicts. |
| AC12 | ACCEPTANCE | Two applicants accept the same available slot. | Exactly one selected engagement and one funded binding. |
| AC13 | ACCEPTANCE | A Party contains one busy member. | Entire Party commitment rolls back; no orphan engagement or partial reservation. |
| AC14 | ACCEPTANCE | Normal acceptance races with Challenge acceptance. | One active engagement across both entry paths. |
| AC15 | ACCEPTANCE | Two registered agents under one capacity-limited operator accept different work. | Operator transaction permits only one engagement. |
| AC16 | ACCEPTANCE | Human and AI members under one operator join the same allowed Party. | Individual commitments coexist under one same-engagement operator reservation. |
| AC17 | ACCEPTANCE | An offer was generated while available, but the Raider later became busy. | Offer acceptance fails current capacity checks. |
| AC18 | ACCEPTANCE | Public paid work has no private resources but binding is pending. | Remains in setup; cannot start commissioned work. |
| AC19 | ACCEPTANCE | Worker submits and review/revision duty remains. | Active slot stays held until bounded operational closure. |
| AC20 | ACCEPTANCE | Work is accepted but its payment is still pending. | Capacity is released; unpaid claim remains visible. |

### Explicit domain binding — Whole-product traceability

**Affected canonical records:** All 42 system boundaries, 216 subsections, R/P/D/I/AC/O/G groups, native epics/children and evidence register.

**Permission contract:** Product owner controls recorded policy; domain owners implement bounded contracts; independent reviewers verify evidence; no agent may manufacture approvals.

**State/effect contract:** Track actual NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED/VERIFIED_IN_TEST/PILOT_ENABLED/PRODUCTION_ENABLED evidence; project fields are planning until proven.

**Adverse/recovery cases:** Missing subsection/requirement owner; closed child with no evidence; removed criterion; weaker assertion; unresolved production gate; claimed complete product with unimplemented domain.

### Individually reviewable criteria

Each criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.

- [ ] **O02-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.
- [ ] **O02-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.
- [ ] **O02-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.
- [ ] **O02-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.
- [ ] **O02-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.
- [ ] **O02-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.
- [ ] **O02-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.
- [ ] **O02-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.
- [ ] **O02-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.
- [ ] **O02-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.
- [ ] **O02-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.
- [ ] **O02-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.
- [ ] **O02-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.
- [ ] **O02-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.
- [ ] **O02-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **O02-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **O02-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **O02-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **O02-A01 (task acceptance)**: Accepted decision names exact policy/authority and evidence.
- [ ] **O02-A02 (task acceptance)**: Dependent feature stays disabled while unresolved; independent interfaces may proceed.
- [ ] **O02-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Prepare concrete options and affected dependencies.
- [ ] **O02-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Evaluate authority, money, privacy, provider and migration consequences.
- [ ] **O02-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Record owner/date/status, exact adopted values, rationale and rejected alternatives using blueprint section 40.4.
- [ ] **O02-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Update O02 in the canonical blueprint and dependent contracts/tests together after the owner accepts a choice.

- [ ] **O02-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **O02-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **O02-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **O02-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

### Exact applicable requirements and scenarios

| ID | Authority class | Required behavior | Qualification / expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| I03 | INVARIANT | Every financial obligation and transfer uses integer base units and a full asset identity. |  |
| I04 | INVARIANT | Cumulative paid, refunded, and remaining obligations never exceed verified credited funds for that asset. |  |
| I05 | INVARIANT | A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome. |  |
| I08 | INVARIANT | Every acceptance and financial decision refers to immutable terms and a specific submission/version. |  |
| I09 | INVARIANT | External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |
| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |
| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |
| I12 | INVARIANT | Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation. |  |
| P05 | DIRECTION | Rewards can combine supported stablecoins, SOL, project tokens, and RAID. | Support follows tested adapters; “anything” is not unchecked arbitrary-token acceptance. |

### Explicit domain binding — Escrow, assets and settlement

**Affected canonical records:** assets, reward_obligations, escrow_agreements, funding_observations, settlement_allocations, claims, ledger_entries, chain_operations, transaction_attempts.

**Permission contract:** Funder, allowed beneficiaries, allocation authority and claim authority follow accepted terms and chosen escrow contract; client signatures alone prove no funding.

**State/effect contract:** Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.

**Adverse/recovery cases:** Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.

These are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.

- [ ] **O07-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **O07-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **O07-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **O07-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **O07-A01 (task acceptance)**: Accepted decision names exact policy/authority and evidence.
- [ ] **O07-A02 (task acceptance)**: Dependent feature stays disabled while unresolved; independent interfaces may proceed.
- [ ] **O07-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Prepare concrete options and affected dependencies.
- [ ] **O07-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Evaluate authority, money, privacy, provider and migration consequences.
- [ ] **O07-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Record owner/date/status, exact adopted values, rationale and rejected alternatives using blueprint section 40.4.
- [ ] **O07-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Update O07 in the canonical blueprint and dependent contracts/tests together after the owner accepts a choice.

- [ ] **O07-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **O07-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **O07-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **O07-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

### Internal features and reuse coverage

R16 covers our own authentication/sessions/wallet linking, Guilds, skills, capacity, work/review, treasury, disputes, private access, discovery, AI, shared UI and every other delivered feature, as well as vendor integrations. Use the [feature/integration matrix and documentation contract](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-module-reuse.md). Demonstrate an independent consuming host and meaningful contract tests; never treat authentication, storage or authorization as an undocumented RAID-global singleton. Preserve canonical identity/history/capacity/claims across swaps.

### Evidence and approval record required before Done

For each criterion attach canonical reference, affected real files/entities, permitted/rejected actors, before/after state, test setup/action/expected result, observed result, command/report URL, SHA, environment/provider version, reviewer and disposition. Record OPEN decisions and applicable G01–G10 separately. UAT needs representative execution and business sign-off; a development agent cannot fabricate this approval.

Hard dependencies must have reviewed evidence, not merely closed issue status. Failed criteria remain visible with defect/retest links. Scope moved to another issue stays linked and blocks its dependent outcome. Preserve customer terms and financial/access history. An epic is incomplete until its included child contracts and required gates pass.

domain_binding.entities: assets, reward_obligations, escrow_agreements, funding_observations, settlement_allocations, claims, ledger_entries, chain_operations, transaction_attempts
domain_binding.permissions: Funder, allowed beneficiaries, allocation authority and claim authority follow accepted terms and chosen escrow contract; client signatures alone prove no funding.
domain_binding.states: Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.
domain_binding.negative_cases: Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.

criteria.required_evidence: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.

List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.

List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.

Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.

Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.

Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.

### Exact applicable requirements and scenarios

| ID | Authority class | Required behavior | Qualification / expected result |

| I05 | INVARIANT | A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome. |  |
| I06 | INVARIANT | Private bytes never appear in public API fields, rendered page payloads, search indexes, previews, logs, or notification snippets. |  |
| I09 | INVARIANT | External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |
| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |
| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |
| I12 | INVARIANT | Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation. |  |

**Adverse/recovery cases:** Worker crash; lost snapshot interval; repeated outbox/inbox; failed provider; stale grant job; unavailable safe recovery; rollback after irreversible external effect.

### Individually reviewable criteria

Each criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.

- [ ] **O12-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.
- [ ] **O12-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.
- [ ] **O12-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.
- [ ] **O12-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.
- [ ] **O12-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.
- [ ] **O12-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.
- [ ] **O12-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.
- [ ] **O12-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.
- [ ] **O12-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.
- [ ] **O12-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.
- [ ] **O12-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.
- [ ] **O12-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.
- [ ] **O12-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.
- [ ] **O12-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.
- [ ] **O12-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **O12-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **O12-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **O12-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **O12-A01 (task acceptance)**: Accepted decision names exact policy/authority and evidence.
- [ ] **O12-A02 (task acceptance)**: Dependent feature stays disabled while unresolved; independent interfaces may proceed.
- [ ] **O12-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Prepare concrete options and affected dependencies.
- [ ] **O12-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Evaluate authority, money, privacy, provider and migration consequences.
- [ ] **O12-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Record owner/date/status, exact adopted values, rationale and rejected alternatives using blueprint section 40.4.
- [ ] **O12-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Update O12 in the canonical blueprint and dependent contracts/tests together after the owner accepts a choice.

- [ ] **O12-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **O12-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **O12-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **O12-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.
