### Individually reviewable criteria

Each criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.

- [ ] **T053-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.
- [ ] **T053-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.
- [ ] **T053-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.
- [ ] **T053-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.
- [ ] **T053-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.
- [ ] **T053-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.
- [ ] **T053-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.
- [ ] **T053-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.
- [ ] **T053-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.
- [ ] **T053-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.
- [ ] **T053-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.
- [ ] **T053-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.
- [ ] **T053-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.
- [ ] **T053-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.
- [ ] **T053-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **T053-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **T053-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **T053-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **T053-A01 (task acceptance)**: Rank/holder status alone cannot read code
- [ ] **T053-A02 (task acceptance)**: All public rendering/search/preview paths stay clean
- [ ] **T053-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Implement PUBLIC/TRUSTED/CONFIDENTIAL/INVITE_ONLY projections
- [ ] **T053-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Approve scoped private scoping brief for informed consent
- [ ] **T053-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Require separate code/resource permission after verified work binding

- [ ] **T053-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **T053-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **T053-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **T053-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

- [ ] **T061-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.
- [ ] **T061-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.
- [ ] **T061-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.
- [ ] **T061-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.
- [ ] **T061-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.
- [ ] **T061-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.
- [ ] **T061-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.
- [ ] **T061-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **T061-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **T061-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **T061-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **T061-A01 (task acceptance)**: Forged familiar-name callback rejected
- [ ] **T061-A02 (task acceptance)**: Model swap does not reset history/capacity
- [ ] **T061-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Store accountable operator, authenticated runtime and versioned capability evidence
- [ ] **T061-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Preserve performance across aliases/model changes
- [ ] **T061-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Issue authenticated short-lived task credentials and callback validation

- [ ] **T061-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **T061-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **T061-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **T061-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

### Evidence and approval record required before Done

For each criterion attach canonical reference, affected real files/entities, permitted/rejected actors, before/after state, test setup/action/expected result, observed result, command/report URL, SHA, environment/provider version, reviewer and disposition. Record OPEN decisions and applicable G01–G10 separately. UAT needs representative execution and business sign-off; a development agent cannot fabricate this approval.

Hard dependencies must have reviewed evidence, not merely closed issue status. Failed criteria remain visible with defect/retest links. Scope moved to another issue stays linked and blocks its dependent outcome. Preserve customer terms and financial/access history. An epic is incomplete until its included child contracts and required gates pass.

domain_binding.negative_cases: Prompt injection; private egress; model/config alias identity; operator conflict; spend cap across retries; unused budget refund; failed cancellation cannot strand capacity.

criteria.required_evidence: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.

### Explicit domain binding — Managed AI runtime and economics

**Affected canonical records:** agent_profiles, participants, agent_runs, run_tool_calls, budget_reservations, usage_ledger, operator_commitments.

**Permission contract:** Policy-enforcing service validates scoped tools/grants/budget outside the model; no self-review, withdrawal, autonomous permission escalation or spend increase.

**State/effect contract:** PLANNED/BUDGET_RESERVED/QUEUED/RUNNING/SUBMITTED with cancellation/failure; run state separate from work/review/billing; total retries/subagents respect common budget.

**Adverse/recovery cases:** Prompt injection; private egress; model/config alias identity; operator conflict; spend cap across retries; unused budget refund; failed cancellation cannot strand capacity.

These are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.

### Individually reviewable criteria

Each criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.

- [ ] **T064-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.
- [ ] **T064-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.
- [ ] **T064-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.
- [ ] **T064-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.
- [ ] **T064-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.
- [ ] **T064-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.
- [ ] **T064-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.
- [ ] **T064-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.
- [ ] **T064-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.
- [ ] **T064-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.
- [ ] **T064-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.
- [ ] **T064-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.
- [ ] **T064-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.
- [ ] **T064-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.
- [ ] **T064-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **T064-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **T064-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.

- [ ] **T064-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Reserve total cap across model/tools/retries/subcalls

Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **T066-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **T066-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **T066-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **T066-A01 (task acceptance)**: Worker cannot approve own reward or promote own rank
- [ ] **T066-A02 (task acceptance)**: One pilot task reaches review with costs/failures visible
- [ ] **T066-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Explain bounded recommendation/capability/cost assumptions
- [ ] **T066-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Use human/Party fallback when skill/data/tool fit fails
- [ ] **T066-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Submit versioned artifacts and ordinary criterion-based review

- [ ] **T066-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **T066-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **T066-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **T066-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

### Evidence and approval record required before Done

For each criterion attach canonical reference, affected real files/entities, permitted/rejected actors, before/after state, test setup/action/expected result, observed result, command/report URL, SHA, environment/provider version, reviewer and disposition. Record OPEN decisions and applicable G01–G10 separately. UAT needs representative execution and business sign-off; a development agent cannot fabricate this approval.

Hard dependencies must have reviewed evidence, not merely closed issue status. Failed criteria remain visible with defect/retest links. Scope moved to another issue stays linked and blocks its dependent outcome. Preserve customer terms and financial/access history. An epic is incomplete until its included child contracts and required gates pass.

domain_binding.states: PLANNED/BUDGET_RESERVED/QUEUED/RUNNING/SUBMITTED with cancellation/failure; run state separate from work/review/billing; total retries/subagents respect common budget.
domain_binding.negative_cases: Prompt injection; private egress; model/config alias identity; operator conflict; spend cap across retries; unused budget refund; failed cancellation cannot strand capacity.

criteria.required_evidence: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.

List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.

List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.

Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.

Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.

Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.

Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.

Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.

Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.

Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.

Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.

### Exact applicable requirements and scenarios

| ID | Authority class | Required behavior | Qualification / expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC15 | ACCEPTANCE | Two registered agents under one capacity-limited operator accept different work. | Operator transaction permits only one engagement. |
| AC16 | ACCEPTANCE | Human and AI members under one operator join the same allowed Party. | Individual commitments coexist under one same-engagement operator reservation. |
| AC61 | ACCEPTANCE | AI reaches total budget across retries/subagents. | Further spend blocked; no autonomous budget expansion. |
| AC62 | ACCEPTANCE | AI tries to approve its own output or withdraw reward. | Permission denied; ordinary authorized review required. |
| AC63 | ACCEPTANCE | Agent changes model/version to evade failure history/capacity. | Canonical identity/commitment retained; evaluation policy applies. |
| AC64 | ACCEPTANCE | Failed/cancelled AI run leaves an active engagement. | Bounded recovery or operational closure; no indefinite slot lock. |
| I01 | INVARIANT | The database rejects a second active engagement for the same canonical participant. |  |
| I02 | INVARIANT | Party activation either reserves every participant or reserves none. |  |
| I03 | INVARIANT | Every financial obligation and transfer uses integer base units and a full asset identity. |  |
| I04 | INVARIANT | Cumulative paid, refunded, and remaining obligations never exceed verified credited funds for that asset. |  |
| I05 | INVARIANT | A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome. |  |
| I06 | INVARIANT | Private bytes never appear in public API fields, rendered page payloads, search indexes, previews, logs, or notification snippets. |  |
| I07 | INVARIANT | No background score change, token sale, or service outage grants code access or confiscates a reward. |  |
| I08 | INVARIANT | Every acceptance and financial decision refers to immutable terms and a specific submission/version. |  |
| I09 | INVARIANT | External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |
| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |
| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |
| I12 | INVARIANT | Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation. |  |
| P01 | DIRECTION | Humans, registered AI agents, and AI influencers are distinct participant types. | Common work contracts; different proof and execution needs. |
| P08 | DIRECTION | AI assistance should reduce founder configuration work. | Explanations and founder control remain visible. |
| R06 | LOCKED | Skill rank represents demonstrated capacity, not token wealth or paid placement. | C05 |

### Explicit domain binding — Managed AI runtime and economics

**Affected canonical records:** agent_profiles, participants, agent_runs, run_tool_calls, budget_reservations, usage_ledger, operator_commitments.

**Permission contract:** Policy-enforcing service validates scoped tools/grants/budget outside the model; no self-review, withdrawal, autonomous permission escalation or spend increase.

**State/effect contract:** PLANNED/BUDGET_RESERVED/QUEUED/RUNNING/SUBMITTED with cancellation/failure; run state separate from work/review/billing; total retries/subagents respect common budget.

**Adverse/recovery cases:** Prompt injection; private egress; model/config alias identity; operator conflict; spend cap across retries; unused budget refund; failed cancellation cannot strand capacity.

These are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.

### Individually reviewable criteria

Each criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.

- [ ] **T084-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.
- [ ] **T084-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.
- [ ] **T084-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.
- [ ] **T084-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.
- [ ] **T084-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.
- [ ] **T084-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.
- [ ] **T084-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.
- [ ] **T084-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.
- [ ] **T084-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.
- [ ] **T084-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.
- [ ] **T084-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.
- [ ] **T084-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.
- [ ] **T084-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.
- [ ] **T084-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.
- [ ] **T084-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **T084-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **T084-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **T084-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **T084-A01 (task acceptance)**: Every listed scenario has actual result and artifact
- [ ] **T084-A02 (task acceptance)**: Mocks cannot replace concurrency/program/effective-access/restore evidence
- [ ] **T084-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Read each listed AC required result
- [ ] **T084-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Use real DB/program/provider/sandbox boundary where the scenario requires it
- [ ] **T084-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Record candidate SHA, fixture/network, command/result and fix/retest for failures

- [ ] **T084-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **T084-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **T084-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **T084-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

### Internal features and reuse coverage

R16 covers our own authentication/sessions/wallet linking, Guilds, skills, capacity, work/review, treasury, disputes, private access, discovery, AI, shared UI and every other delivered feature, as well as vendor integrations. Use the [feature/integration matrix and documentation contract](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-module-reuse.md). Demonstrate an independent consuming host and meaningful contract tests; never treat authentication, storage or authorization as an undocumented RAID-global singleton. Preserve canonical identity/history/capacity/claims across swaps.

### Evidence and approval record required before Done

For each criterion attach canonical reference, affected real files/entities, permitted/rejected actors, before/after state, test setup/action/expected result, observed result, command/report URL, SHA, environment/provider version, reviewer and disposition. Record OPEN decisions and applicable G01–G10 separately. UAT needs representative execution and business sign-off; a development agent cannot fabricate this approval.

Hard dependencies must have reviewed evidence, not merely closed issue status. Failed criteria remain visible with defect/retest links. Scope moved to another issue stays linked and blocks its dependent outcome. Preserve customer terms and financial/access history. An epic is incomplete until its included child contracts and required gates pass.

domain_binding.permissions: Domain owners define commands; operations have scoped repair authority; development access does not imply customer or treasury authority.
domain_binding.states: Additive migration/backfill; immutable terms and semantic IDs survive rollback/restore; constraints and outbox are established before dependent slices.
domain_binding.negative_cases: Legacy obligations survive migration; crash after external success; restore with missing recent acceptance; same idempotency key with altered request.

criteria.required_evidence: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.

List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.

List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.

Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.

Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.

Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.

Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.

Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.

Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.

Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.

Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.

domain_binding.entities: assets, reward_obligations, escrow_agreements, funding_observations, settlement_allocations, claims, ledger_entries, chain_operations, transaction_attempts
domain_binding.permissions: Funder, allowed beneficiaries, allocation authority and claim authority follow accepted terms and chosen escrow contract; client signatures alone prove no funding.
domain_binding.states: Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.
domain_binding.negative_cases: Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.

criteria.required_evidence: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.

List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.

List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.

Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.

Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.

Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.

Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.

Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.

Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.

Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.

Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.

List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.

Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.

Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.

### Explicit domain binding — Managed AI runtime and economics

**Affected canonical records:** agent_profiles, participants, agent_runs, run_tool_calls, budget_reservations, usage_ledger, operator_commitments.

**Permission contract:** Policy-enforcing service validates scoped tools/grants/budget outside the model; no self-review, withdrawal, autonomous permission escalation or spend increase.

**State/effect contract:** PLANNED/BUDGET_RESERVED/QUEUED/RUNNING/SUBMITTED with cancellation/failure; run state separate from work/review/billing; total retries/subagents respect common budget.

**Adverse/recovery cases:** Prompt injection; private egress; model/config alias identity; operator conflict; spend cap across retries; unused budget refund; failed cancellation cannot strand capacity.

These are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.

Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.
- [ ] **G01-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.
- [ ] **G01-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.
- [ ] **G01-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.
- [ ] **G01-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.
- [ ] **G01-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.
- [ ] **G01-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.
- [ ] **G01-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **G01-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **G01-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **G01-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **G01-A01 (task acceptance)**: All required gate evidence is linked and reviewed.
- [ ] **G01-A02 (task acceptance)**: No mock/unit-only/merge result is claimed as production assurance.
- [ ] **G01-A03 (task acceptance)**: Unpassed dependent feature remains disabled.
- [ ] **G01-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Collect the canonical gate evidence: Approved protocol, parameters, verified IDs, authority/fee behavior, recovery.
- [ ] **G01-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Name tested/deployed SHA, environment/network, provider/program version and operating owner.
- [ ] **G01-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Review meaningful adverse/recovery results and outstanding decisions.
- [ ] **G01-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Record go/limited-go/no-go; update the evidence register and exact feature flag scope.

- [ ] **G01-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **G01-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **G01-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **G01-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

### Evidence and approval record required before Done

For each criterion attach canonical reference, affected real files/entities, permitted/rejected actors, before/after state, test setup/action/expected result, observed result, command/report URL, SHA, environment/provider version, reviewer and disposition. Record OPEN decisions and applicable G01–G10 separately. UAT needs representative execution and business sign-off; a development agent cannot fabricate this approval.

Hard dependencies must have reviewed evidence, not merely closed issue status. Failed criteria remain visible with defect/retest links. Scope moved to another issue stays linked and blocks its dependent outcome. Preserve customer terms and financial/access history. An epic is incomplete until its included child contracts and required gates pass.

Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.
- [ ] **G04-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **G04-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **G04-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **G04-A01 (task acceptance)**: All required gate evidence is linked and reviewed.
- [ ] **G04-A02 (task acceptance)**: No mock/unit-only/merge result is claimed as production assurance.
- [ ] **G04-A03 (task acceptance)**: Unpassed dependent feature remains disabled.
- [ ] **G04-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Collect the canonical gate evidence: Exact registry, decimals/program checks, extension policy, complete tested paths.
- [ ] **G04-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Name tested/deployed SHA, environment/network, provider/program version and operating owner.
- [ ] **G04-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Review meaningful adverse/recovery results and outstanding decisions.
- [ ] **G04-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Record go/limited-go/no-go; update the evidence register and exact feature flag scope.

- [ ] **G04-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **G04-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **G04-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **G04-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.

### Internal features and reuse coverage

R16 covers our own authentication/sessions/wallet linking, Guilds, skills, capacity, work/review, treasury, disputes, private access, discovery, AI, shared UI and every other delivered feature, as well as vendor integrations. Use the [feature/integration matrix and documentation contract](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-module-reuse.md). Demonstrate an independent consuming host and meaningful contract tests; never treat authentication, storage or authorization as an undocumented RAID-global singleton. Preserve canonical identity/history/capacity/claims across swaps.

### Evidence and approval record required before Done

For each criterion attach canonical reference, affected real files/entities, permitted/rejected actors, before/after state, test setup/action/expected result, observed result, command/report URL, SHA, environment/provider version, reviewer and disposition. Record OPEN decisions and applicable G01–G10 separately. UAT needs representative execution and business sign-off; a development agent cannot fabricate this approval.

Hard dependencies must have reviewed evidence, not merely closed issue status. Failed criteria remain visible with defect/retest links. Scope moved to another issue stays linked and blocks its dependent outcome. Preserve customer terms and financial/access history. An epic is incomplete until its included child contracts and required gates pass.

domain_binding.entities: assets, reward_obligations, escrow_agreements, funding_observations, settlement_allocations, claims, ledger_entries, chain_operations, transaction_attempts
domain_binding.permissions: Funder, allowed beneficiaries, allocation authority and claim authority follow accepted terms and chosen escrow contract; client signatures alone prove no funding.
domain_binding.states: Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.
domain_binding.negative_cases: Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.

criteria.required_evidence: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.

List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.

- [ ] **G07-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.
- [ ] **G07-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.
- [ ] **G07-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.
- [ ] **G07-A01 (task acceptance)**: All required gate evidence is linked and reviewed.
- [ ] **G07-A02 (task acceptance)**: No mock/unit-only/merge result is claimed as production assurance.
- [ ] **G07-A03 (task acceptance)**: Unpassed dependent feature remains disabled.
- [ ] **G07-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Collect the canonical gate evidence: Operator identity, sandbox, tool authority, spend controls, provider data policy.
- [ ] **G07-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Name tested/deployed SHA, environment/network, provider/program version and operating owner.
- [ ] **G07-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Review meaningful adverse/recovery results and outstanding decisions.
- [ ] **G07-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Record go/limited-go/no-go; update the evidence register and exact feature flag scope.

- [ ] **G07-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.

- [ ] **G07-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.

- [ ] **G07-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.

- [ ] **G07-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.
